title: Hook work runs in the resident: cache on its store, persist only what must outlive it
body:
Cache hook-path work on the resident's store, not in the hook process. Hooks are thin clients: src/hooks/run.js posts session-start, prompt and pre-tool to the machine's resident (callRunningStore), which keeps one store per project open across calls, so an in-memory cache on that store does hit between tool calls while the resident lives. When no resident answers, pre-tool exits without retrieval and the other events only do bookkeeping, so do not optimize the local hook path. Persist in the SQLite index (index_meta through store.index.getMeta/setMeta, as projectContext() in src/engine/project-context.js does) only when the value must survive a resident restart or be shared with the separate MCP server process.

Why: The previous version said a property on the store dies with each hook process and cited projectContext's in-memory cache as the bug. Since the shared resident, every hook that retrieves is answered by that long-lived process (run.js returns the bridged reply before opening a store, and skips pre-tool when nothing answers), and projectContext now caches in index_meta. Optimizing the per-event Node process buys nothing.

evidence.summary: A bridged reply is returned before openStore; without one, pre-tool is skipped unless DD_RETRIEVAL=lexical.
hookProject keys projects by repo root and reuses the store it already opened.
projectContext caches in index_meta via store.index.getMeta('project_context').

v1.trigger: Reviewing or optimizing PreToolUse/observe/prompt hook cost, or adding a cache on the store object anywhere in src/engine or src/hooks.
